messages.subject: Default hyperparameters for the "copy" model
parts:
Hi INLA team, a hopefully quick question.  I am getting confused about the meaning of the hyperparameters in the "copy" model.  In the following example, is this setting the precision or the variance to 10 for the Gaussian prior of the hyperparameter of the copied model?

formula <- y~ -1 + f(xi.field,model=spde) + f(x.field,copy="xi.field",fixed=FALSE, hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(-1,10))))


Many thanks,

Penny Hancock

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Default hyperparameters for the "copy" model
parts:
On Fri, 2017-11-03 at 08:33 -0700, Penny Hancock wrote:
> Hi INLA team, a hopefully quick question. I am getting confused
> about the meaning of the hyperparameters in the "copy" model. In the
> following example, is this setting the precision or the variance to
> 10 for the Gaussian prior of the hyperparameter of the copied model?
>
> formula <- y~ -1 + f(xi.field,model=spde) +
> f(x.field,copy="xi.field",fixed=FALSE,
> hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(-1,10))))

Hi Penny,

when doing a copy, there is a hyperparamter, which will scale the copy, like

beta * x

and you can set a prior for beta,

use

hyper = list(theta = list(
fixed = FALSE,
prior = "gaussian",
param = c(mean, precision)))

H
